Consider the following initial value problem for the functions $y=y(x),z=z(x),w=w(x):$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}=x+y+{w}^{2},\, & y(0)=1 \\ {z}^{′}=2y-z,\, & z(0)=2 \\ {w}^{′}=-w+xz,\, & w(0)=1\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method.
What entries should be placed in the columns for $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ in the table below if the step size is $Δx=1?$

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ |  |  | {{field-1}} |  |  | {{field-2}} |  |  | {{field-3}} |

feedback.worked_solution:
Euler's method approximates the solution of an initial value problem containing a system of ODEs by applying the update rule component-wise to each equation.

First, because the initial conditions are $y(0)=1,$ $z(0)=2,$ and $w(0)=1,$ we place $y=1,$ $z=2,$ and $w=1$ in the table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ |  |  | $2$ |  |  | $1$ |  |  |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′},{z}^{′},$ and ${w}^{′}$ according to the given rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x+y+{w}^{2} \\  & =0+1+{1}^{2} \\  & =2 \\ {z}^{′} & =2y-z \\  & =2\cdot 1-2 \\  & =0 \\ {w}^{′} & =-w+xz \\  & =-1+0\cdot 2 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |  | $2$ | $0$ |  | $1$ | $-1$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy,$ $Δz,$ and $Δw$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx=2\cdot 1=2 \\ Δz & ={z}^{′}\cdot Δx=0\cdot 1=0 \\ Δw & ={w}^{′}\cdot Δx=(-1)\cdot 1=-1\end{aligned}
$$

We add these to our table.

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-1$ |

To get the new values of $x,$ $y,$ $z,$ and $w$ in the *next* row, we add $Δx$ to $x,$ $Δy$ to $y,$ $Δz$ to $z,$ and $Δw$ to $w,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=0+1=1 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy=1+2=3 \\ {z}_{\text{new}} & =z+Δz=2+0=2 \\ {w}_{\text{new}} & =w+Δw=1+(-1)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these values to our table in a new row gives the following:

| $x$ | $y$ | ${y}^{′}$ | $Δy$ | $z$ | ${z}^{′}$ | $Δz$ | $w$ | ${w}^{′}$ | $Δw$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $0$ | $0$ | $1$ | $-1$ | $-1$ |
| $1$ | $3$ |  |  | $2$ |  |  | $0$ |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that
$y(1)≈3,$
$z(1)≈2,$
and
$w(1)≈0.$
